Built: all 41 tables read via introspection (information_schema + pg_constraint) against the live schema through legion_reader, matching the table count and names execution-plan.md lists; server/legacy/ app with one managed=False model per table, split into fleet/ledger/pantry/ingest/dates/notes/places/body/memory/household.py under legacy/models/ (one app, ten files, not ten apps - domains stay grouped for readability, app_label is 'legacy' throughout); legacy/enums.py (Provenance, IngestState TextChoices hand-correcting inspectdb's USER-DEFINED blind spot); legacy/CONSTRAINTS.md listing every live CHECK constraint by table. manage.py check clean; makemigrations --check clean (required MIGRATION_MODULES = {'legacy': None} - managed=False alone does NOT suppress makemigrations, only migrate's DDL, confirmed the hard way); ruff check server clean. Phase-0 update mid-session: LEGION_PG_ADMIN_URL (legion_engine) arrived, so ticket 01's four owed checks (login wrong/right/revoked, healthz) now ran for real via pytest-django's own ephemeral test database (never the live 'postgres' database) - all pass, 48/48 total, JUnit XML confirms 0 errors/0 failures/0 skipped. Building this exposed and fixed two real bugs, both left in server/legion/settings.py with a comment: (1) _parse_database_url did not percent-decode username/password, so any credential containing a URL-reserved character (this project's did) authenticated as garbage and tripped Supabase's pooler circuit breaker - fixed with urllib.parse.unquote(); (2) routing Django's own tables to a 'django' schema by nesting the schema-creation RunSQL inside household's own migration chain broke AUTH_USER_MODEL's swappable-dependency resolution ('Related model household.user cannot be resolved') - fixed by moving it to a new model-less core app (core/apps.py explains why). INCIDENT: the legion_reader password appeared in plaintext in one verbose pytest traceback in the agent's own tool output before the decode bug was found and fixed; recommend rotating that credential. Did NOT run manage.py migrate against the live admin 'postgres' database itself (only the throwaway pytest test database) - creating permanent household/auth/session tables in the shared production Postgres ahead of ticket 04's API design felt like a bigger, harder-to-reverse call than this session's brief covered; surfaced rather than decided. tickets.title: The domain API: one resource shape for 38 tables, a changes feed, idempotent upsert by origin_guid
tickets.detail: Phase 2 slice built: /api/events, /api/checklists (+items, +ticks), /api/changes, all behind DeviceTokenAuthentication+IsHouseholdMember. checklists is a new Django-managed app (Checklist/ChecklistItem/ChecklistTick, public schema via a temporary search_path swap in its own migration, touch_updated_at + measured-tick-guard triggers). events sits over the existing legacy.Event (managed=False). Built against this ticket's own dispatch brief, which scopes the endpoint shapes to POST+PATCH+soft-DELETE for the two Phase 2 aspects - narrower, and shaped differently (no PUT-by-origin_guid upsert), than this file's own generic 38-table SyncedModelViewSet text below, which predates the phase split in research/execution-plan.md. Not done: the other 36 tables, server/api/COVERAGE.md, the openapi.yaml-staleness test, /api/dates/events/<id>/skips/. 45 new tests green, 0 failures (JUnit: 86 total, 41 skipped - the pre-existing legacy-readonly suite, gated on LEGION_PG_URL). Baseline before this ticket: 48 total (7 passed, 41 skipped). A test-only mirror of public.events'/event_skips' DDL was added to tests/conftest.py so pytest's ephemeral database (which never runs legacy's Supabase-owned migrations) has something to write against - flagged for a second look since every future ticket writing to a legacy table (ledger, pantry, fleet) hits the same wall. PHASE 5 (2026-09-06): the generic SyncedModelViewSet this file describes now exists (server/api/synced.py) and four aspects are registered on it - places (keyed by label), voice_notes (keyed by the server id, POST creates, PUT never inserts, no audio field on the wire), body (all eight tables: workout_plans, workout_plan_items, workout_set_logs, bodyweight_logs, meal_targets, meal_logs, sleep_targets, sleep_logs) and memory (memories, companion_memories, memory_audit - the last append-only, no DELETE route, 405 in words). Thirteen tables, 26 routes, generated from api/registry.py, which api/changes.py reads too so the feed and the routes cannot drift; /api/changes now accepts aspects=events,checklists,places,voice_notes,body,memory. Test-database DDL for the thirteen legacy tables is tests/legacy_test_schema.py - the shared version of the conftest events mirror flagged above; ledger, pantry and fleet still owe theirs. api/sync.paginate_since now renders its `next` cursor Z-suffixed via DRF's DateTimeField instead of Python isoformat's +00:00, which a client could not hand back unencoded. 250 tests pass, 0 failures (baseline measured before this pass: 86 collected, 86 passed with LEGION_PG_URL set - NOT the 93 the dispatch brief stated). NOT routed, deliberately: ledger and pantry (both wait on the section 4 gate moving server-side, ticket 03) and fleet (four identity shapes, obd_samples at 20,796 rows needs a windowed pull and batched upload). Still not done from this ticket's own list: server/api/COVERAGE.md, openapi.yaml and its staleness test, /api/dates/events/<id>/skips/, and the events/vehicles PUT-by-either-key form. Two findings worth a human's eyes, both in this pass's report: the Django host's clock and Postgres's differ by ~0.5s so the new serializers stamp created_at/updated_at with SQL Now() rather than timezone.now() (api/events.py still uses the Python clock), and test_events_api.py's since-feed tombstone test mixes the two clocks - it passes in a full run and fails when run alone. SCHEMA PASS (2026-09-07): server/openapi.yaml is written and committed, regenerated by `cd server && uv run manage.py write_openapi` (a new management command - it resolves the path from BASE_DIR so cwd cannot change where it writes, and passes --fail-on-warn and --validate, so a view drf-spectacular cannot describe is an error rather than a path missing from the contract). tests/test_openapi_schema.py holds the staleness test, a security-scheme check, and four checks that compare the schema against REAL responses; proven both ways (green as committed, red with a named first-differing line after a serializer was perturbed, reverted). Generator errors went 92 (15 unique) to 0 and warnings 63 (29 unique) to 0: api/schema.py adds the DeviceTokenAuthentication security extension (without it the document had NO security: at all, so a generated client would not know the Authorization: Token header exists), a SyncedAutoSchema that describes all 13 synced tables from their own serializer, and the shared 400/404/since/active pieces; every plain APIView got @extend_schema; settings gained ENUM_NAME_OVERRIDES for the two different `provenance` choice sets (the collision was being resolved as a hash-named `Provenance382Enum`). 63 operations, 42 paths, valid OpenAPI 3.0.3. THE SCHEMA LIED ABOUT EVERY LIST ROUTE and nothing caught it: DRF renders `{results, next}` and drf-spectacular's list-action heuristic documented a BARE ARRAY of rows - confirmed against the deployed engine, not inferred, which is why three of the new tests diff declared properties against a real call. Two more findings for a human: /api/ingest/statement and /api/ingest/receipt answer Django's own 404 on the DEPLOYED engine (legion-757959564788.us-south1.run.app still runs a pre-ingest revision - the schema describes the code, the deploy is behind it), and POST /api/auth/logout with no body and no Content-Length is answered 411 by Cloud Run's frontend before it reaches Django, so the token is NOT revoked. Also still unimplemented from this file's own text: the X-Legion-Api response header and the major-version refusal (grep finds it nowhere in server/ or app/). Still not done: server/api/COVERAGE.md, /api/dates/events/<id>/skips/, the events/vehicles PUT-by-either-key form, and ledger/pantry/fleet routes. Ingest request bodies are described as free-form JSON objects with their keys listed in prose, deliberately: the body IS the RPC payload and ingest/views.py reads it key by key, so a serializer written only to describe it would be a second description free to drift from the reads. FLEET PASS (2026-09-07): fleet is routed and every aspect now has an API. server/api/fleet.py holds eleven tables on the generic SyncedModelViewSet across FIVE identity shapes - origin_guid (vehicles, service_history), sync_id (drives, code_events, code_clear_events, oil_analyses, build_entries, drive_reassignments), a natural text primary key (chassis_quirks), a primary key that is also a foreign key (vehicle_specs), and the COMPOSITE (vehicle_id, service_name) (maintenance_schedules) - plus obd_samples on three hand-written routes of its own. TWO tables did not fit the generic shape and are written out rather than bent onto it. (1) maintenance_schedules keeps the generic list feed but has its own two-segment detail path /api/fleet/maintenance_schedules/<vehicle_id>/<service_name>/ and its own upsert/destroy/_lookup; SyncedModelViewSet gained detail_path_suffix() and identity_path_parameters() hooks for it, and api/schema.py now builds a LIST of path parameters instead of one hardcoded `identity`. It stays in api/registry.py on purpose - the registry is what makes routed and in-the-changes-feed the same fact. (2) obd_samples is not in the registry at all: no serverId, no tombstone column, 20,796 rows live, a windowed per-vehicle pull and a batched upload. GET /api/fleet/obd_samples/ REQUIRES ?vehicle=<uuid> (400 naming it when absent, 404 when it names no vehicle, never an empty page) and windows on recorded_at via ?since=; the 30-day window stays the CLIENT's choice, not a narrowing the server applies. POST .../batch/ takes a JSON array capped at 1000 (twice the phone's 500) and is idempotent on the natural key (vehicle_id, pid, recorded_at) through one raw INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id, answering {received, inserted, already_present, duplicates_in_batch}; a re-post inserts nothing and answers 200 rather than 201. GET .../count/ replaces countObdSamples and takes an OPTIONAL vehicle. There is no DELETE and no detail route anywhere on obd_samples. /api/changes?aspects=fleet returns ELEVEN keys and never obd_samples - the feed is unpaged, so folding telemetry in would make a bare GET /api/changes a whole-archive download; the exclusion is stated in api/registry.py, api/changes.py, api/fleet.py AND the `aspects` parameter description in openapi.yaml. Two small shared changes were forced by fleet and are worth knowing: SyncedSerializer.create only mints an `id` when the model HAS one (chassis_quirks and vehicle_specs have no separate id column, and objects.create(id=...) on either was a TypeError, i.e. a 500); and the append-only 405 wording moved out of SyncedModelViewSet into a per-viewset no_delete_reason, because \"it is an audit trail\" is true of memory_audit and false of a spec sheet - memory_audit sets the same sentence it always had. tests/legacy_test_schema.py gained its FOURTH block, LEGACY_FLEET_TEST_SCHEMA_SQL, all twelve fleet tables with every CHECK, every unique constraint, every FK and the touch_updated_at trigger on the eleven that have updated_at; it keeps obd_samples_natural_key_idx because that index IS the batch endpoint's idempotency and a test database without it would prove the opposite of what the test claims. Reading the live schema rather than the migration files turned up one discrepancy worth a human's eyes: vehicles.archived, vehicles.last_obd_mac and maintenance_schedules.never_done DEFAULT FALSE are all present on the live database while all three migration files still say \"UNAPPLIED as of this commit\" in their own headers. 146 new tests, 589 total, 0 failures, 0 skipped (JUnit XML, LEGION_PG_URL set). openapi.yaml regenerated: 85 paths, 119 operations, no list route typed as a bare array (checked programmatically across every path, not just the new ones). STILL NOT DONE from this ticket's own list, unchanged by this pass: server/api/COVERAGE.md, /api/dates/events/<id>/skips/, the events/vehicles PUT-by-either-key form (the vehicles half of that row is what this pass did NOT build - only the origin_guid key), the X-Legion-Api header and the major-version refusal. NEW and owed: there is no server-side retention on obd_samples - nothing deletes an old row and the server holds every sample ever uploaded, growing at the phone's ~600/day. That is what makes the \"phone is a cache\" ruling work, so it needs a ruling of its own rather than an implementation detail buried here. TWO EXISTING TESTS were corrected rather than suppressed, and the correction is the point: tests/test_changes_api.py's two unknown-aspect tests both sent aspects=fleet as their stand-in for a name this server does not know, because fleet was the last unrouted aspect. Routing it made both go green-to-red with 200 != 400, which is exactly what those tests exist to do; the example moved to a name that is not an aspect and will not become one, and the second test now also asserts `fleet` appears in the list of known ones. Their docstrings carry the history - this is the second time that example has had to move (it was `ledger` before it was `fleet`), and it should be the last, since there are no unrouted aspects left.

tickets.title: Whitenoise, a multi-stage arm64 image with the Vite build, migrate-on-start, and Caddy on the domain
tickets.detail: Built 2026-09-08. `server/Dockerfile` is now two stages: `node:24-slim` runs `npm ci` and `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) in `frontend/`, whose committed `outDir: '../static/app'` resolves to `/static/app` inside the container, and the python stage takes it with `COPY --from=frontend` and runs `collectstatic` with the five `required_env` variables inline on that one RUN - never as `ENV`, which would have baked a throwaway SECRET_KEY into the running image and turned `required_env`'s loud failure into a silent default. supercronic is per-arch on `TARGETARCH` with both SHA1s pinned (amd64 `e63c11a9...`, unchanged; arm64 `0b6c5bb743e0b0dafed1132198c81807927ac413`, new), each confirmed twice: downloaded and `sha1sum`ed, and read off aptible's v0.2.49 release notes. `TARGETARCH` carries a default of amd64 because `gcloud builds submit` (the Cloud Run rollback path) runs the classic builder, which never sets it. New `server/.dockerignore` keeps the developer's own `static/app` and `staticfiles` out of the context - without it `COPY . .` lays a stale build down and `collectstatic` ships a mix of two. `deploy/Caddyfile` is `{$LEGION_DOMAIN::80} { reverse_proxy web:8000 }` with a quoted `email \"{$LEGION_ACME_EMAIL}\"` global; `caddy` in compose gained `env_file: .env` without which both substitutions are empty inside the container and the stack silently serves plain HTTP forever. **The entrypoint is `server/entrypoint.sh`, NOT `deploy/entrypoint.sh` as this ticket and ticket 13 both say.** It cannot live in `deploy/`: the Docker build context is `server/` in all three places that build this image (compose's `web` and `worker`, and `deploy/cloudrun/deploy.py`'s `docker build server/` and `gcloud builds submit server/`), a `COPY ../` is not expressible, and Cloud Build does not support BuildKit named contexts. Whoever writes ticket 13's runbook must use `server/entrypoint.sh`. **VERIFIED WITHOUT DOCKER** (this machine has none): hadolint 2.15.1 exit 0 on the Dockerfile (DL3008/DL4006/DL3059 declined with the reason on the line above each); shellcheck 0.11.0 exit 0 on `entrypoint.sh`; `caddy validate` 2.11.4 `Valid configuration` with the two variables both set and both unset, plus `caddy fmt` clean - and it was that run which proved an UNQUOTED `email {$LEGION_ACME_EMAIL}` is a hard startup failure when empty; the compose YAML parses and every service still carries a profile with the worker's supercronic entrypoint override intact; the inline-env `RUN` form was executed in a real `sh` to prove all five variables reach the command. **THE IMAGE HAS NEVER BEEN BUILT.** Not for arm64, not for amd64, not at all - so `collectstatic` has never run in the container, the `COPY --from=frontend /static/app` path has never been resolved by Docker, and `npm ci` has never run against `node:24-slim`. This ticket's own 'done means' (a `linux/arm64` build, plus a `--profile full up` serving `/`, `/static/app/*.js` with `max-age=31536000, immutable`, and `/api/auth/me`) is entirely UNMET and is owed on the first machine with Docker - the VM in ticket 13, or any laptop with it installed. The latency baseline this ticket asks for is a headed but empty section in `deploy/vm/README.md`, marked NOT MEASURED YET, because there is no box to measure.
